sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-92. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kinuku. p.47 reports 2016 survey data collected on 'Nu (=Kinuku)'; Table 1 (p.48) lists Nu as 'Vigorous', source 'Blench (2016)' which is absent from the reference list (unpublished survey data). The phonology section describes Boze only (four level tones plus glides); no stress statement for any Kauru-subgroup language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (entry 353 'Nu'); also ed. 3 (2012) entry 243 'Kinuku'.

sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives names (Tinu, Binu/Anu; Kinugu, Kinuka, Kinuku), location (Kaduna State, Saminaka LGA, c. seven villages), population 3000 (est. 2016), classification, status 'Vigorous', 'Source: Blench (2016)'. No wordlist, grammar or phonology reference is listed.
